notes.chapter: Cap. 2: Rock around the click: la electrónica de los setenta, de Hallogallo al ambient en la era del Moog (1968-1982)
notes.text: Término de la prensa inglesa que los grupos rechazan («un concepto de márketing», Roedelius). Kraftwerk y su sociedad mecanizada, el ritmo motorik de Neu! en «Hallogallo» —para Eno, uno de los tres ritmos más inventivos de los setenta junto al afrobeat de Fela Kuti y el funk de James Brown—, las exploraciones de Can en su estudio Inner Space, Faust, Amon Düül II, Popol Vuh, Cluster y Harmonia, con Conny Plank como productor clave. Su huella más clara: el post-rock de los noventa (Stereolab, Tortoise, Radiohead).

refs.q: El ritmo creado por Neu! es uno de los tres más inventivos de los setenta
refs.para: El ritmo creado por Neu! es uno de los tres más inventivos de los setenta junto al afrobeat de Felá Kuti y el funky-beat de James Brown.
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Rock around the click: la electrónica de los setenta, de Hallogallo al ambient en la era del Moog (1968-1982)

refs.q: un concepto acuñado por la prensa inglesa que todos los grupos rechazan
refs.para: …máquina («The Robots»), al profundo e hipnótico concepto del ritmo dibujado por Neu! en su primera composición («Hallogallo»), pasando por las exploraciones casi antropológicas de Can por las músicas de todas las latitudes (africana, tango, cha-cha-cha, reggae, árabe, sinfónica, blues, jazz, hard rock), la psicodelia desde la Baja Baviera que perpetraron Amon Düül II, la música cósmica de Ash Ra Tempel, los efluvios planeadores de Tangerine Dream y Klaus Schulze, las partituras impresionistas de Popol Vuh —la banda sonora de Aguirre, la cólera de Dios (1974), de Werner Herzog, es tan alucinante y neblinosa como la mente perturbada del conquistador Lope de Aguirre que encarna Klaus Kinski—, las experimentaciones de Cluster o Harmonía hasta la libertad expresiva de Faust. El llamado krautrock (un concepto acuñado por la prensa inglesa que todos los grupos rechazan; según Hans-Joachim Roedelius, de Cluster, no deja de ser «un concepto de márketing», una palabra que sirvió «para definir a los grupos alemanes que en la época practicaban rock en la onda anglosajona e incorrecto para capturar lo que nosotros hacíamos») fue una incesante fuente de hallazgos sonoros en los que la electrónica tuvo, en líneas generales, una función capital. «Nos abrió las puertas de la percepción», argumenta Roedelius, y por eso abundaron los grupos de teclados y los de instrumentación a priori más ortodoxa, que también franquearon con talento las delimitadas fronteras…
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Rock around the click: la electrónica de los setenta, de Hallogallo al ambient en la era del Moog (1968-1982)

refs.q: Stereolab, Tortoise, UI y otros grupos actuales como Radiohead parten de rítmica y matices sonoros próximos a Can
refs.para: El legado de Can ha resistido cualquier tipo de erosión provocada por el paso del tiempo. PiL —su bajista, Jah Wobble, es colaborador habitual de Czukay y Liebezeit—, Brian Eno, Bill Laswell, The Fall, Julián Cope y Thin White Rope son algunos nombres que asumen la deuda contraída, aunque donde más se ha notado la huella de aquellas bandas alemanas de la época ha sido en el post-rock en los noventa: Stereolab, Tortoise, UI y otros grupos actuales como Radiohead parten de rítmica y matices sonoros próximos a Can y, especialmente, a Neu!

similar_scenes.name: Krautrock y motorik
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: Los ritmos «motorik» teutónicos de Kraftwerk y Neu! y la improvisación disciplinada de Can. Para muchos postpunks el single más significativo de 1977 no fue «White Riot» sino «Trans-Europe Express», canto fúnebre metronómico para la era industrial: una visión de la Neue Europa moderna, auténticamente postrock, sin deuda con la música estadounidense.
similar_scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

similar_scenes.name: Kosmische Musik y krautrock
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: El rock británico recicla el americano; el alemán inventa otro tipo de rock (a menudo, ni siquiera rock). Los músicos alemanes ven la relación entre la psicodelia y la vanguardia electrónica de Stockhausen: en 1968 nace el Zodiak Free Arts Lab de Berlín, en 1969 debutan Can, en 1971 Tangerine Dream inventan la «kosmische musik» con sintetizadores y secuenciadores y el viaje del acid-rock se convierte en viaje por el cosmos; en 1972 la larga suite electrónica (Zeit, Irrlicht) fija el formato que se copiará treinta años. Amon Duul II (gótico teutón), Can (el estudio del ritmo y la textura: Tago Mago, Future Days), Holger Czukay (world music electrónica), Tangerine Dream, Klaus Schulze, Ash Ra Tempel, Guru Guru, Agitation Free y otros. Ningún movimiento, salvo los primeros rockeros, influyó en tantos músicos durante tantas décadas.

similar_scenes.name: Krautrock: Cluster, Kraftwerk, Faust y Neu!
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: Sin interés por la psicodelia ni por el universo, fascinados morbosamente por la psique del siglo XX. Kluster/Cluster pasan de la disonancia electrónica a los drones y al ambient (Zuckerzeit, Harmonia, Grosses Wasser); Kraftwerk funden electrónica, sonido industrial y melodía pop, sustituyen la batería por ritmos electrónicos y engendran a la vez la música industrial y la disco (Autobahn); Faust, el primer grupo «lo-fi», collages expresionistas y una de las visiones más líricas de la alienación moderna; Neu!, el «motorik beat» de Klaus Dinger y la repetición obsesiva.

podcast.title: Attitude Towards Experimentation
podcast.body: Krautrock contributed to tracing the experimental attitude that defined post-rock, following earlier influences like The Velvet Underground. "Then we trace this attitude towards experimentation through things like crowd rock, David Bowie, public image limited, and the no wave seen in New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Bowie's "Krautrock Muse"
podcast.body: David Bowie actively followed his "Krautrock Muse," heavily influenced by German bands like Kraftwerk, Can, and Neu!, which shaped the sound of his Berlin albums "Low" and "Heroes." "Bowie continued to follow his Crout Rock Muse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bowie's Berlin Period Fascination
podcast.body: By 1977, David Bowie had grown fascinated with German krautrock bands such as Can, Neu!, and Kraftwerk. This genre, along with electronic music, heavily influenced his "Berlin period" albums, which saw him and collaborators Brian Eno and Tony Visconti incorporating these sounds as Bowie aimed for a personal and career reset. "He had also grown fascinated with electronic music and German crowd rock, bands like Cannes, Noy, and of course, Croftvirk."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Characterized by Specific Elements
podcast.body: Krautrock is identifiable by its unique sound, which includes a distinct beat, the pervasive use of electronics, an "icy coldness," a sometimes droning approach, tasteful improvisations, and a deliberate departure from rock's traditional rhythm and blues roots. These elements allowed it to work its way into many forms of rock. "The beat, the use of electronics, the icy coldness, the sometimes use of a drony approach, the tasteful improvisations, and above all, a move far, far away from rock's traditional roots, which of course is rhythm and blues."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Declining Influence on Lodger
podcast.body: David Bowie's *Lodger* album marked a departure from previous works in the Berlin Trilogy by having significantly fewer influences from classic German Krautrock bands. "no tiene tantas influencias de esas bandas clásicas del que Rock Aleman."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: David Bowie: La trilogía de Berlin 3

podcast.title: Early Influence on David Bowie
podcast.body: Krautrock bands like Kraftwerk and Neu! were significant influences on David Bowie's *Station to Station* album and continued to immerse him during his Berlin residency. "principalmente de Crawford y no hoy quienes ya habían sido una gran influencia para Station to Station."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El proyecto que salvó a David Bowie. La trilogía de Berlín

podcast.title: German Origins (1970s)
podcast.body: Krautrock emerged in West Germany during the 1970s, as German musicians sought to distance themselves from their country's Nazi past by creating a distinct German rock style, different from UK and American music. "The next step on the post rock ladder is probably the music that came out of West Germany in the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: German Rock Movement
podcast.body: Described as "that very German sort of rock that came about in the 1970s," Krautrock is a genre of particular interest to Johnny Greenwood of Radiohead. "Crot Rock, that very German sort of rock that came about in the 1970s"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Depeche Mode's Ultra
podcast.body: Krautrock, along with German industrial music, exerted important influences on Depeche Mode's album Ultra. This genre contributed to the album's powerful bases and deep electronic sounds, moving away from traditional synthesizers towards more complex, computerized structures. Its integration showcased the band's openness to new artistic directions after a critical period. "Incluso como el Cloud Rock y la música alemana industrial que tiene influencias muy importantes con esas bases tan potentes, esos unidos electrónicos están profundos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Depeche Mode -  Ultra. Punto de inflexión de la banda

podcast.title: Influence on Electronic Music
podcast.body: Krautrock is mentioned as an influence on the sound of Boards of Canada, contributing to their unique electronic style. "tiene influencias de Brian Eno, de tangera indream del crowd rock."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: BOARDS OF CANADA. La visión romántica del IDM

podcast.title: Influence on Joy Division
podcast.body: Krautrock was a key influence on Joy Division's sound, especially as guided by producer Martin Hannett. Hannett steered the band towards a sound that sometimes approached Krautrock, alongside other experimental electronic music styles. "los aferca a veces incluso al Crab Rock."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Influence on Post-Punk
podcast.body: Krautrock began to make serious inroads into the UK after British labels like Virgin Records signed numerous bands, viewing it as a form of prog rock. This exposure significantly changed post-punk music in the country, influencing its sound with icy coldness, hypnotic rhythms, and electronic elements. "This is how crop rock started to make serious inroads into the UK, inroads that changed post-punk music in the country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Post-punk
podcast.body: Krautrock was a significant influence on post-punk bands like Joy Division, contributing to their experimental, non-instrumental, and background soundscapes. "tenía influencias del crowd rock, tenía influencias de can, tenían influencias de pin flow y de la velvet underground"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 1. Inicios en la escena post-punk

podcast.title: Influences and Approaches
podcast.body: This music blended psychedelic rock and electronic music, bravely exploring approaches not rooted in the traditional blues and R&B of standard rock. "They liked psychedelic rock and electronic music. And they were brave enough to try approaches that weren't necessarily rooted in the blues and R&B traditions of standard rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Diffusion (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: In the late 1970s, German Krautrock had significant diffusion within Europe, but its reach was considerably limited outside the continent. While some bands like Kraftwerk were known in the United States, the genre did not achieve widespread mainstream success or major chart presence there.

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: David Bowie: La trilogía de Berlin 2

podcast.title: Legado Electrónico
podcast.body: El Krautrock, específicamente su vertiente más electrónica como la de crowdwork (Kraftwerk), es mencionado como parte de los movimientos y artistas que, con tecnología más avanzada, reinterpretaron el Space Age Pop en épocas posteriores, siguiendo la senda experimental. "el crowd rock más electrónico de crowdwork"

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Así sonaba el pop de la era atómica

podcast.title: Nomenclature: "Kajshmi music" vs. "Krautrock"
podcast.body: Germans initially called it "Kajshmi music" (cosmic music), but a "cheeky Brit" coined the name "Krautrock," which ultimately stuck. "The Germans called it Kajshmi music, cosmic music. But then some cheeky Brit decided it should be called Kratrock and that name stuck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins of the Name
podcast.body: The name "Krautrock" was coined by the British, initially as a pejorative term derived from "Sauer Kraut," a slur for Germans dating back to World War II. It began as an insult, evolved into a joke, and then, as the music gained traction, it stuck and became highly respected, despite many Germans finding it insulting and an unnecessary throwback to the war years. "But it was the Brits who came up with a name that stuck, Crout Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Persistent Influence on David Bowie's *Lodger*
podcast.body: The influence of Krautrock remained very present in David Bowie's *Lodger* album, which also incorporated New Wave, World Music, and pop sounds. "con la influencia del Craw Rock, aún muy presente."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El proyecto que salvó a David Bowie. La trilogía de Berlín

podcast.title: Post-War Cultural Rebirth
podcast.body: Krautrock's story is deeply intertwined with Germany's post-World War II context, serving as a political, demographic, social, and artistic effort by Germany to rebuild after the Nazi past. The genre wouldn't exist without the foundational events of WWII and the subsequent desire for a new cultural identity. "Craftrock's story is especially interesting because of its origins as a political, demographic, social, and artistic attempt by Germany to rebuild after a Nazi past."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unpopular in Germany, Popular Abroad
podcast.body: For a considerable period, Krautrock bands struggled to gain recognition or commercial success within Germany itself, with German labels hoping for a "German version of The Beatles." However, these acts garnered significant attention outside the country, particularly in the UK, where labels eagerly signed them. "One of the interesting things about crop rock is how, for the longest time, none of these homegrown bands could get arrested in Germany."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Varieties and "Motorik" Rhythm
podcast.body: Krautrock encompassed various styles, from electronic-focused (like Kraftwerk) to noise-preferred material with a driving, hypnotic 4/4 rhythm known as "motorik," which evoked driving on the Autobahn. "There are many different varieties of Kratrock. Some went all in with electronics like craft work. There's like noise preferred material with a driving hypnotic, 4-4-rhythm known as motoric, which evoke driving in a car in the Autobahn."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
